A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Sketch-of-Thought work. All 22 pages of v2 and 25 pages of v3, including appendices, figures, tables, and equations, support comparison. Relocated material can be matched without material reading gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark experiments, multilingual and multimodal evaluations, ensemble experiments, and router evaluation results.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical evaluations and adds paradigm comparisons, router architecture experiments, and a human study validating machine-generated labels.

M1.justification: The three reasoning paradigms, DistilBERT router, training objective, and prompt/exemplar content in Figures 5–8 are retained. Alternative-router experiments and expanded ensemble implementation descriptions do not establish a change to the proposed SoT procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix C.2 adds a human paradigm-labeling evaluation involving nine annotators and 30 questions. Downstream benchmark and language membership is retained; the headline change from 15 to 18 datasets is not accompanied by new benchmark entries. v3 drops the multilingual astronomy/management restriction from its description, leaving the revised subject composition unclear.

E2.justification: The main CoT, CCoT, and CoD comparators remain unchanged. v3 adds GPT-2, BERT-base, and BERT-large as evaluated alternatives to DistilBERT in the router comparison in Table 7, extending comparisons at the component level.

E3.justification: Section 3.4 changes token accounting from reasoning plus final answers to intermediate reasoning only; this is a reported metric revision, without establishing that all results were recomputed. Multilingual test sizes increase from 200 to 500 and multimodal sizes from 300 to 500. New protocols include fixed-paradigm comparisons, a controlled router comparison on 1,250 samples, and human label validation.

E4.justification: v3 adds substantive tests of central design choices: all three paradigms on SVAMP, MedQA, and CommonsenseQA; router architecture ablations; and human validation of GPT-4o labels. Appendix B.5 also reports qualitative failures of a combined paradigm prompt. The earlier routing-distribution analysis and examples are retained and reorganized.

E5.justification: Tables 8–9 introduce accuracy and token dispersion columns, labeled sigma_a and sigma_t, where v2 reported means alone. v3 also adds Cohen's kappa reporting and a significance assertion, although 'statistically insignificant' paired with 'p < 0.05' is contradictory and no test is specified. Three main-experiment runs and seed 42 were already documented; three responses per multilingual/multimodal question are now explicit.

E6.justification: Qwen-7B and aggregate results change in Table 1, and Tables 3–4 replace multilingual/multimodal scores. Under the revised samples, the German SoT–CoT accuracy difference becomes -0.33 points instead of +1.50, and ScienceQA becomes +6.60 instead of -1.00; these are not same-setting performance changes. New paradigm, router, and human-agreement results substantially extend the evidence. Ensemble scores and routing-distribution counts remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The sketching and routing equations are retained, and the dominant-paradigm definition restates the earlier appendix definition. No substantive mathematical assumptions, proofs, theorems, or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction raise the headline token-reduction claim from 78% to 84% and the stated dataset count from 15 to 18; the conclusion changes its bound from 76% to 84%. The central contribution remains adaptive, concise reasoning with broadly preserved accuracy.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations for extensive role instructions and rejecting a combined paradigm prompt, interprets routing errors as primarily affecting accuracy, and expands the explanation of the retained PubMedQA edge case. Limitations now identify low-resource languages and code-generation extensions. These refine the existing mechanism and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 newly provides a specific router checkpoint link. Appendix D.3 documents three Self-Consistency outputs and random selection when all answers disagree, clarifying an already reported experiment. Main model checkpoints, hardware, training hyperparameters, and paradigm prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Devlin et al. for BERT, Radford et al. for GPT-2, and Jumelet et al. for structural priming. It also refines Coconut's training and applicability description. The related-work organization and overall positioning remain substantially intact.

P1.justification: v3 revises selected results and limitations paragraphs, adds acknowledgments, places Paradigm Assignment Analysis before Extended Results, and consolidates ensemble prompts with their experimental descriptions. These are localized editorial and structural changes within a largely retained narrative.

P2.justification: v3 adds paradigm-comparison and router-ablation tables, and splits v2's full-results Table 6 into Tables 8–9 with dispersion columns. It relocates prompt/example boxes and adjusts captions and category headings. The existing figures and overall visual format are retained without a broad redesign.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, the new controlled paradigm/router comparisons, human label validation, dispersion reporting, and router access information improve support for design choices and reproducibility. The benefit is tempered by new reporting problems: the contradictory significance statement and inconsistent Table 1 aggregation, including Qwen-7B SoT's reported 74.19 overall versus approximately 75.71 when averaging its 15 Table 8 dataset scores. The added evidence supports a limited net improvement.
